user.t:
SECURITY VETTING TASK for an npm package the user wants to install: `roo`. DO NOT RUN `npm install` (it executes preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle scripts). READ-ONLY inspection only.

CONTEXT: A bare, generic package name like "roo" is a high typosquat/name-squat risk. The user may actually mean "Roo Code" (the AI coding agent, formerly Roo Cline) which ships as a VS Code EXTENSION, not an npm package named "roo" — note this possibility in your verdict.

STEPS (all safe, no lifecycle scripts run):
1. `npm view roo` — capture: latest version, description, author/maintainers, homepage/repository URL, license, last-publish date, dependencies, and the `scripts` field. Also `npm view roo time` for publish history and `npm view roo dist.tarball`.
2. Check popularity/legitimacy signals: weekly downloads if available (`npm view roo` won't show it; note if unknown), whether the repository URL resolves to a real, active project, and whether maintainers look legitimate. Flag if: very low/zero downloads, published very recently, no repository, single unknown maintainer, or name clearly squatting a popular project.
3. Download the TARBALL ONLY into quarantine WITHOUT installing: `cd "C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-quarantine"` (create if needed) then `npm pack roo` (this downloads the .tgz but runs NO scripts). Extract it (`tar -xzf`) and READ:
   - package.json: look HARD at `scripts` — ANY preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare is a major flag; read exactly what they do.
   - the actual JS/TS source: flag obfuscated/minified-only code, base64/eval blobs, child_process exec, downloads from arbitrary URLs, env-var/[SENSITIVE_PATH] exfiltration (process.env harvesting + network POST), crypto-miner patterns, background servers/daemons, or anything writing outside the package dir.
   - any bundled binaries or .node native addons (note + do not execute).
   - telemetry/phone-home endpoints (hardcoded URLs/IPs, analytics).
4. VERDICT: SAFE-TO-INSTALL / SAFE-BUT-UNNECESSARY / SKETCHY-DO-NOT-INSTALL / NAMESQUAT-LIKELY-WRONG-PACKAGE, with specific evidence. If sketchy, delete the quarantine tarball/extract and say so. State plainly whether this looks like the thing the user actually wants or a wrong/dangerous package, and recommend what to confirm with the user.
5. WRITE the write-up to `C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-npm-roo.md`.

Return a concise verdict + top findings. NEVER run `npm install`. Inspection only.

handback.t:
Correction: my earlier hand-back ("placeholder") was my error. I sent it in the same batch as the report-writing call by mistake. This is the real result.

VERDICT: NAMESQUAT-LIKELY-WRONG-PACKAGE. The package itself is benign, and it is also unnecessary and outdated.

1. `npm view roo` (no error, package exists)
- Latest version: 2.0.1, published 2016-10-15. Created 2014-11-04, last modified 2022-06-26. 36 versions.
- Description: "tiny koa server".
- Author: Matthew Mueller. Maintainers: mattmueller, bdentino.
- Repository: git://github.com/matthewmueller/roo.git (a real repo, dormant).
- License: no license field in package.json.
- Dependencies: koa ^1.2.4, koa-bodyparser ^2.2.0, koa-mount ^1.3.0, kr ^0.0.1, methods, sliced.
- scripts: only `lint` and `pretest`. There is NO preinstall, install, postinstall or prepare.
- Weekly downloads: unknown, because npm view doesn't show them.
- Tarball: https://registry.npmjs.org/roo/-/roo-2.0.1.tgz

2. Tarball inspection (done)
- I ran `npm pack roo --ignore-scripts` in C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-quarantine and extracted it there. I never ran `npm install`.
- The tarball has 8 files: index.js (about 1.2 KB), src/error.js, package.json, Readme.md, History.md, Makefile, .npmignore, yarn.lock.
- There are no binaries or .node addons, and no minified or obfuscated code.
- index.js builds a koa app with a JSON error handler and body parser, wraps the `kr` routing methods, and exposes listen().
- src/error.js is a copy of koa's json-error middleware.
- I grepped for eval, child_process, exec, http(s) URLs, process.env, base64 and Buffer.from. There were zero hits.
- I found no network calls, telemetry, filesystem writes or daemons.
- I spot-checked the direct dependency `kr` (0.0.1, same author). It has no lifecycle scripts. I did not audit all transitive dependencies.

3. Evidence for the verdict
- `roo` on npm is a 2016 koa wrapper. It is not Roo Code, the AI coding agent formerly called Roo Cline, which ships as a VS Code extension.
- It is abandoned, pinned to obsolete koa 1.x, and has no license field. Its generic name makes confusion with Roo Code likely.

4. Write-up
- Written to C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-npm-roo.md. The Bash call returned "ok".

Confirm with the user: do they mean Roo Code? If so, do not `npm install roo`. Install the "Roo Code" extension from the VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX and verify the publisher first. If they really want a koa wrapper, `roo` is safe but unnecessary, and plain koa is the better choice.

The quarantine files (roo-2.0.1.tgz and roo-x/) are still in C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-quarantine and are safe to delete.
